detail: Arcana: Books on the Arts is a rare/specialty art-book shop, not a curated exhibition space; its website and events page show book launches and signings rather than art exhibitions.
Cherry and Martin closed permanently in 2018; the space at 2712 S. La Cienega Blvd was rebranded as Philip Martin Gallery, which is already on the saved-venues list.
Gallery's own exhibitions page shows its last show ("And After: Group Exhibition") ran 3 July - 22 August 2026, now past, with no future exhibition listed or announced as of Sept 1, 2026.
Klowden Mann permanently closed in 2020; LinkedIn/Facebook and gallery archives confirm it operated 2010-2020 and is no longer an active gallery. Website (klowdenmann.com) is currently unreachable.

Site footer states 'Open by appointment only, Tuesday - Saturday 10am-5pm' — no public walk-in hours confirmed, and site functions primarily as an online shop for a single featured artist's works rather than a curated public exhibition.
Cultural bookstore/community space with no confirmed gallery exhibitions currently or within 60 days
Artforum listing shows no exhibitions currently listed; nonprofit performance/exhibition space between shows
Educational arts center focused on classes and youth programming, not a public exhibition gallery
Artist-run space is currently archival with no exhibitions; future page shows outdated content (2020 projects coming soon)
Main venue at 1300 E 1st St closed to public for building renovations; exhibitions are at traveling locations not the home venue
Last exhibition (Streets, Structures & Stories) ended July 25, 2026; no upcoming shows confirmed on site within 60-day window
Website is stub with no current exhibitions; Wikipedia indicates founder moved to Mexico in 2021; cannot confirm current operations
Gallery listed as open by appointment only with no public walk-in hours; no current or upcoming exhibitions on programming page
Gallery located at 2525 Michigan Avenue, Santa Monica, CA (not Culver City/West Adams); also open by appointment only with no confirmed upcoming exhibitions
Most recent show, "MY KARMA RAN OVER MY DOGMA," was a one-weekend pop-up that closed Aug 30, 2026; site's homepage shows no confirmed next exhibition or reopening date as of Sep 1, 2026.
Last posted exhibition, "The Body, As Sculpture, As A Crow," ran June 12 - July 12, 2026; no new show or opening date posted on the venue's own site or Facebook page since.
No official website could be located (noustous.co is inaccessible, formal exhibition listings are years out of date); could not confirm any current or upcoming exhibition from a primary source.
Site's "Current" exhibition page still shows "e/Crit-s," which ran 03/21/26-04/25/26 and has long closed; no newer show or opening date posted on the gallery's own site as of Sep 1, 2026.

Anat Ebgi has relocated its LA gallery from 2660 S. La Cienega Blvd to 6150 Wilshire Blvd, Suite 5, Los Angeles (Mid-Wilshire/Miracle Mile). The gallery's own exhibitions page lists only "Wilshire" (6150 Wilshire Blvd) and "Tribeca" (NYC) locations — no Culver City/West Adams space remains, so it no longer belongs in this zone.

Blum & Poe (rebranded BLUM) permanently closed its brick-and-mortar Los Angeles gallery at 2727 S. La Cienega Blvd; Tim Blum announced in July 2025 that he was stepping away and shuttering the LA and Tokyo spaces entirely, ceasing public exhibition operations. The gallery's own website is unreachable (expired SSL cert) and Yelp lists the location as "BLUM - CLOSED."

Edward Cella Art & Architecture no longer operates the 2754 S. La Cienega Blvd space; per the gallery's own contact page it now shows work only "@ Thomas Lavin Showroom" inside the Pacific Design Center (8687 Melrose Ave / Sunset Blvd mailing address), which is outside the Culver City/West Adams corridor. Its current-exhibitions page also returns no listed shows.

Sixty29 Contemporary's own contact page states "OPEN BY APPOINTMENT" for its 6029 Washington Blvd location; it is described as the private studio of artist Carlo Marcucci with no public walk-in hours, so it doesn't qualify for the public-facing guide.

Confirmed upcoming show on the gallery's own site: Nathan Vincent, "The Shape of Awareness," Sept 8 - Oct 31, 2026, opening reception Sat Sept 19, 4-7pm, at 2642 S. La Cienega Blvd. However the gallery's dated, hotlink-protected website only serves thumbnail-scale artwork images (largest found was 450x600px for the show's hero image; other artist-page images top out around 166x200px), and no higher-resolution version could be found via press, Artsy, or the artist's own site for this specific exhibition.

No independent website; only a Facebook/Instagram presence. The only "current" show findable, "Meet Me At The Boulevard," is actually a 2024 group exhibition (confirmed via a participating artist's own events page) — the Facebook post touting it as "current" is stale. Could not confirm any real on-view or upcoming show, current hours, or gallery operating status from a primary source.

Gallery's own website (coagulacuratorial.com and its square.site mirror) returns server errors / renders no exhibition content on every page attempted (home, /about, /current). No current or upcoming exhibition could be confirmed from the venue's own site; secondary sources (Artsy, Wikipedia, LA Art Show) only describe the gallery historically with no current show listed.

Gallery's own domain (markjudegallery.com) displays a "coming soon" placeholder with no content. Press coverage from July 2025 describes the grand-opening show (Antonio Kim, Caterina Piccardo, Samuel Scharf, Megan Mueller) but gives no indication of what, if anything, is currently on view over a year later, and hours were only ever "Saturdays and by appointment." Could not confirm a current or upcoming exhibition from a primary source.
Keystone Gallery's own exhibition calendar shows its last listed show ("Vestiges" by Alexandra Lopez Iglesias) ran September 12-20, 2026 — wait, this is confirmed and upcoming.
